ref.substituent_description: A long unbranched zigzag chain starting at Et runs to an NH that forms an amide C(=O) to a benzene ring; para to the amide, the ring carries a CH2CH2 chain attached to C4 of a piperidine. The piperidine N is part of a urea N-C(=O)-NH to a second benzene ring that carries an NMe2 group para to the urea NH.
ref.notes: Typeset drawing. Double bonds: two C=O (amide and urea) plus two benzene rings with 3 each. The chain between Et and NH has about ten zigzag vertices.

wrong.substituent_description: An Et label at the left end of a zigzag chain of 10 line vertices ending at an NH, which is bonded to a C(=O) attached to a circle-depicted benzene ring; para (position 4) to that carbonyl is a CH2CH2 chain leading to the 4-position of a piperidine. The piperidine N is bonded to C(=O)-CH2 attached to a second circle-depicted benzene ring bearing, para (position 4) to the CH2, an N carrying two Me labels.
wrong.notes: Handwritten black ink on grey paper photographed at a slight angle. Two C=O double bonds drawn as paired strokes. NH is written with H stacked above N. The chain vertex count (10) is between the Et label and the NH.

correct.substituent_description: A long zigzag chain of 10 unlabelled vertices runs from Et to an NH, which is bonded to a C(=O) on a circled benzene ring; para (1,4) to it on that ring is a two-carbon CH2CH2 linker to the 4-position of a piperidine. The piperidine N is bonded to a urea C(=O), then NH, then a circled benzene ring that carries N(Me)2 para (1,4) to the NH.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: The zigzag chain length (10 unlabelled vertices between Et and NH) must be counted from the drawing; each vertex is a bend.
correct.notes: Handwritten, small writing on a wide canvas. Two C=O double bonds, no other double bonds; two aromatic circles.

ref.substituent_description: Long unbranched alkyl zigzag chain starting at Et on the left and ending at an amide NH-C(=O) attached to a para-disubstituted benzene ring; the other para position carries a CH2CH2 linker to C4 of a piperidine. The piperidine N is acylated as a urea N-C(=O)-NH attached to a second para-disubstituted benzene whose para position carries N(Me)2.
ref.notes: Typeset structure. Exact number of chain carbons between Et and the amide NH not counted with confidence (roughly ten). Double bonds: 3 in each benzene ring plus 2 C=O.

wrong.substituent_description: An Et group on the end of a long unbranched zigzag chain (about ten unlabelled vertices) ends in an amide NH, C(=O), attached to a para-disubstituted benzene ring (circle). The para position of that ring carries a two-carbon (CH2CH2) linker to C4 of a piperidine whose N is acylated by C(=O)-CH2- attached to a second para-disubstituted benzene ring (circle), whose para position bears an N(Me)2 group.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: exact number of zigzag vertices in the long chain is hard to count
NH written as H stacked above N
wrong.notes: Handwritten, photographed on grey paper. Two C=O double bonds (benzamide C=O and the N-acyl C=O).

correct.substituent_description: A long zigzag unbranched chain (about 11 vertex carbons between Et and NH, exact count uncertain) starts at Et and ends at NH-C(=O)- on a benzene ring (circle). That benzene is para-disubstituted: the amide carbonyl at one vertex and a CH2CH2 (two-carbon) linker at the opposite vertex going to C4 of a piperidine ring (6-membered, one N). The piperidine N is acylated as a urea N-C(=O)-NH- joined to a second benzene (circle) which carries N(Me)2 para to the NH.
overlaps_or_ambiguities: Number of carbons in the long zigzag chain is hard to count exactly (about 11 vertices)
correct.notes: Handwritten, black ink on white; thin line, small dots at some vertices. Double bonds are the two C=O (amide and urea). The N of NMe2 has two separate Me labels.
